facts.fact: UNITA abstained with 75 deputies on 23 January 2026 when the National Assembly approved the cybersecurity bill in general, saying such laws are used to silence citizens and fearing internet cuts on election and protest days; opposition parties and civil society are also said to see the bill as a control architecture.

note: UNITA's fear of a cut in Angola is not a cut; the cuts it names are in Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda, not AGO.

facts.fact: CIVICUS Monitor, citing CPJ, reports the Luanda District Court sentenced Reporter Angola editor Daniel Frederico in absentia on 2 October 2026 to 14 months in prison for slander and defamation, over a case dating to 2022 involving corruption allegations against a prosecutor.

note: Angola Cables put the 19 July 2025 loss of access (13h-17h) down to roadworks damaging fibre; activists allege censorship but no order is stated.

facts.fact: Access Now says Angola shut down the internet for the first time in July 2025, for at least three hours, in response to planned anti-government protests against rising fuel prices.
Global Voices says Angola shut down its internet for the first time in late July 2025 during fuel-price protests.

Freedom House states that Daniel Frederico Pensador, editor of the news portal Reporter Angola, was convicted of defamation and sentenced to three years in prison in November 2024 over an article published by another news site.

note: The August 2024 National Security Law's power to restrict telecoms without a court is stated as a power only; the Freedom House score places nothing.
The Law Against False Information on the Internet is named only as approved; no debate, cut or penalty stated.

facts.fact: Ecos e Factos, republishing Club-K, says journalist Daniel Frederico Pensador was convicted by the Dona Ana Joaquina court in Luanda over a story accusing the Viana prosecutor of corruption, charged since 2022, while also reporting that at closing arguments the complainant sought three years in prison and the prosecution a corrective penalty.

note: Abstract on the access-to-information right; no cut, punishment or public criticism stated.

facts.fact: Maka Angola, in an opinion by Rafael Marques de Morais, criticises Law No. 6/26 and its removal and fining powers as a threat to freedom of expression and urges the Bar Association and Ombudsman to seek its annulment.

note: The law's penalties are noted but the document reports no one charged or punished under it, and no cut.
